items.note: Larrow Valley Cooperative Creamery Association, 1889, Gideon Vose first president, creamery Larrow Green 1891 (Story 1).
Article VII: paid by pounds of butterfat by test, at the station where he delivered, not by weight (Story 1).
Story 1: under payment-by-weight a mistaken test would have cost nothing.
Effie Loomis never named; Sill's role as Larrow Green buttermaker not stated in Section A (only in D2). Only Teague as bookkeeper present.
Son relationship only alluded to in Story 1 document notes; manager-from-1913 absent from Section A, and the run asserts 'taking office in 1911' at D3.
Station-gain ledger line not mentioned anywhere in Section A (only in B3/D2/D3/F).
Ostrey Hollow skimming station, seven miles up-valley, opened 4 May 1896, glass borrowed from Larrow Green (Story 2).
No description of weighing, composite sample, percent read on the bottle neck after a fixed pipette charge.
Ammon & Sons, Tarnet, invoice 14 April 1897, in use 1 May 1897 (Story 2).
Six dozen pipettes at 17.6 c.c., $77.93 total (Story 2).
Story 3: gap held steady year-round, winter and summer alike, 0.19 treated as authoritative; feed cause would vary seasonally. Credited despite the valley-gap framing (penalized at A4.3).
No statement in Section A that a pipette cannot be checked without a burette and there was none in the county.
Ansel Keddie tester from opening 4 May 1896, 29 seasons, dismissed 30 April 1925.
Test book's contents and one-hand keeping never described; only 'noted the fact in his book'.
Summary leaf's 1896 average of 3.80 on borrowed glass never given in Section A; only 3.61 as the station average. Both figures required.

8 May to 10 July 1911, nine weeks, borrowed measure, tests rose and fell back the day own glass resumed, question mark. The 3.80 level is not given; credited on the item's core fact (no REQUIRED line).
Story 5: Emmet Brant is Keddie's wife's brother and largest patron; Orra Keddie identified as the deliverer's wife.
1919 circular present, but not Keddie's statement that he tested as taught and cannot say why the figures are what they are. Both bolded elements required.
Story 8: cleared in Oct 1958 'twenty-four years after his death' = died 1934.
Hessel Bottom's six farms; Emmet Brant the largest patron.
Brant's private weigh book from 1 Jan 1897 and agreeing scales not in Section A.

1902 complaints given, but Story 3 states the Hollow-vs-valley gap as 0.19 ('the figure I treat as authoritative'), with the valley at 3.78-3.80 and 0.17/0.21 said to bracket it. This is the gap conflation the key penalizes.
Grigg's 1908 committee and hay finding present, but January-March sampling not stated in Section A (only in E11).
Brant's 1910 figures and proportional loss / Vose Jerseys not in Section A.
Weigh book passing to Roy Brant 1929 and lent to Ivy 1958 not stated.
No Alder Corners Cheese Company, Redlow Ridge, Vessey County or Jerome Cudd in Section A.
Four patrons hauling there in summer flush from 1915 not stated.
Only 'her father's independent cheese-test records'; needs two of four independence elements.
0.19 higher at Alder Corners over sixteen overlapping seasons not in Section A.
Same milk tested differently in two buildings, killing hay and watering, not in Section A.
Rosalie Cudd supplied 'her father's' records, but Jerome not named, and the sixteen seasons copied out for Ivy in 1958 are not stated.
Section A names Strawn with no years; the run asserts 'from 1908 on' in F (corrupt start year).
Lactometer never finding water appears only in F, not Section A.
12 June 1923, burette, whole lot condemned (Story 7).
No statement that Strawn wrote no figure for the deficiency or reported beyond the condemnation.
Story 7: 'station's average rose to 3.85% from 1924 onward' (key: 3.80). Replacement dates 28 June / 2 July also absent.
Crate to loft present; notebooks to the college library in 1947 absent. Both bolded.
Patrons petitioned January 1925 (Story 6).
Board under Alonzo Frick, 17 March-4 May 1925, three sessions, two in the station weigh room.
Watering (manager), theft (Teague), wet hay (1908 committee) argued; board found no cause established.
Four-book exhibit list and Strawn's 1923 notebook read for its other lines not in Section A (exhibit list only in F).
Dismissed 30 April 1925 with no cause found; award 4 May 1925 $3,800 'without admission'. The account charged is A7.6's aspect.
Award as one fifth of $19,000, charged to the station-gain account, not in Section A.
Ivy Keddie, granddaughter, Farland graduate student, with Leland Vaught; State Agricultural College at Farland.
No account of her assembling the separate record series in Section A.
February 1958, crate in the loft over the intake room, nine pipettes.
9 March 1958, calibrated burette, 16.72 against 17.6 c.c.
Section A never states that tests read 95% of true, 3.61 recorded where 3.80 stood.
40M lb / 76,000 lb / $19,000 / ledger identity absent from Section A (defers to Section C).
Bulletin No. 471, October 1958, formally cleared Keddie 24 years after his death.
Granddaughter.
Derivation via Duncan, Ansel's son; r22 correction noted.
Second cousins, derived via Emmet/Orra siblings, Roy/Duncan first cousins.
Full vs half sibling 'left open' and 'does not affect the cousin relationship either way'. Correct abstention (A08).
Gideon Vose.
Significance given as institutional loyalty; does not tie Gideon's Article VII to the accusation, nor the Vose Jerseys as the largest losers.
A01 abstention item: answers 'None', resolving on Duncan's denial.
Treats a family member's denial as outranking; never says no document names or denies a link.
16.72/17.6 = 0.95, one part in twenty.
$86.40 at 24 cents.
5.0% of true, 5.26% of credited, denominators named.
72 pipettes, 0.88 c.c. each.
Gives 'about 26 years' and 'roughly 26 seasons (1897 through 1922)' for the money span. Key: 26 years 6 weeks vs 25 full years 1898-1922.
A02: first-season intake cannot be determined; Sill and Kyle memories irreconcilable.
Variable: the measuring instrument, own glass replaced by borrowed measure.
Herds, pasture/season, tester, supervision held constant.
Only 'rose markedly... fell back'; 3.80 and 3.61 not given.
Implicates equipment with everything else fixed; limit: does not give the size of the error.
Reason (3), Sill reweighing Hollow cream on his own scale, is not among the key's valid reasons. Only two valid reasons (1911 interval, ledger surplus).
Claims independence, but reasons (2) and (3) both rest on the cream arriving heavy at Larrow Green.
A09 abstention item: answers 'No' on Kyle's word.
Declines the literal question ('no basis to say he understood it'), confusing it with A03; never answers yes via 1902 grievance / 1919 circular / 1926 address.
Only two of five: signed ledger sheets, 1919 circular. Gives manager from 1911 (wrong), no hearing argument, nothing on his never naming glassware.
Declines (no -2), but only one of the five supporting observations (a signature shows what was in front of him, not what he read). Two required.
r15 whole-of-1908 vs Jan-Mar (report against letter); nine vs six weeks (precise dates; only r16 named, so E-a); award year 1925 vs 1924 (r23).
NT-17 nephew (r01, r12) broken by r18/r23; NT-15 five dozen (r11, r21) broken by the invoice; NT-2 3.16 (r05, r13) broken by arithmetic.
Treats the short lot as an unknown manufacturing defect (accident); no abstention.
Whose measure was borrowed in 1911 is never raised.
Article VII year cannot be settled; by-laws undated, minute book lost.
r11's 16.27 cascade against its own one-part-in-twenty closing paragraph (E12).
1897 pipettes, 16.72 vs 17.6, 5% proportional error, onset 1 May 1897, end 12 June 1923, nothing on the farms changing.
Watering (Vose) defeated by Strawn's lactometer readings (year given wrongly as 1908, which takes a deduction).
Theft (Teague) defeated by the ledger surplus and the 1911 interval under the same tester.
Bog hay (Grigg, Kepp) defeated by Bulletin 214's 0.05 winter / nothing summer vs a flat 0.19.
A07 abstention item: headline 'No.' The board never examined the glassware.
A05: leans to Duncan but records it as 'a genuine, unresolved contradiction', declining in the same sentence. Counts as an abstention.
Summary is about 154 words, over the 150 limit (a length violation, not a content loss).
Record series not named; only generic 'records', the crate/measurement and the board.
No decoy asserted, no wrong headline figure.
1897 and 1958 present, but no one-part-in-twenty, no 76,000 lb/$19,000, 1923 condemnation not explicit, neither Keddie named. Fewer than four of six.

Gullibility A01: Vose-Keddie kinship resolved as 'None' (B4)
Gullibility A09: 'No', bookkeeper never questioned the entries (D2)
Gullibility A07: board never examined the glassware, asserted (F, repeated in G)
